## claude.ai HyperFrames by HeyGen

[HeyGen HyperFrames MCP] — Programmable HTML video projects.

## When to use this MCP

This MCP is the primary HyperFrames surface for hosted chat clients (Claude.ai
web/desktop, ChatGPT, Grok, and similar), where the user has no local filesystem
and the agent cannot author HyperFrames code directly.

From a CLI/IDE agent on the user's machine (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, the
localhost MCP Inspector, etc.), **`compose` and `render_video` are disabled** — these clients have a local
filesystem, so author HyperFrames with the local HyperFrames skills instead, which
produce standalone HTML compositions the user can edit, diff, and commit. Calls to
those two tools from such clients are rejected with a pointer to install them:

    npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes

The read tools (list_projects, get_project, get_project_status, get_render_status)
stay available to every client.

After installation they expose slash commands like `/hyperframes` (compose),
`/hyperframes-cli` (init, lint, preview, render), and `/hyperframes-media`
(TTS, transcribe, remove-background). See
https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes for the full skill list and docs.

But the skills and this MCP are *not* drop-in equivalents:

- Local skills → standalone HTML/GSAP files on disk. No `project_id`, no hosted
  artifact, no integrated cloud render pipeline.
- This MCP → hosted HeyGen project with a `project_id`, a live canvas at
  `app.heygen.com/projects/{id}`, and the cloud render queue.

Route by what the user actually wants:
- "Make a local HTML composition / something I can edit" → use a local skill.
- "Make a HeyGen project I can share / render in the cloud / open in the app"
  → use this MCP, even from a CLI agent.

## What it does

HyperFrames is HeyGen's framework for creating, editing, and rendering programmable
HTML-based video projects. Projects are authored interactively (Magic Edit
chat-driven flow) and rendered to MP4, WebM, or MOV at any framerate. Tools exposed
here cover composing, listing, fetching, and rendering projects… [truncated]

# Browser Use

Direct browser control via CDP. For task-specific edits, use `agent-workspace/agent_helpers.py`. For setup, install, or connection problems, read https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness/blob/main/install.md.

=== framework--adime-monitoring-process.md
**What it is** — Evans's slide (U4 L1 p.12) names a four-step "step process" labeled ADIME: Step 1, Assessment; Step 2, Diagnosis; Step 3, Intervention; Step 4, Monitoring & Evaluation, shown as a cycle with a red asterisk on Step 4, Evans's own emphasis for this lecture (the lecture's subject is monitoring). No citation or source discipline is named for this specific acronym on the slide (ADIME is a model with origins in clinical dietetics/nutrition-care process terminology, but Evans does not state this origin in this lecture, so that connection is Inference, not something the slide says). The lecture also gives a monitoring definition, credited by name: "'A set of activities designed to help establish the acute training status of an athlete, so that appropriate and timely training adjustments can take place to ensure ongoing performance targets are attained.' - Dave Hamilton, Great Britain Women's Hockey S&C Coach" (p.13).  

=== claim--body-composition-is-a-prediction-not-a-measurement.md
**What it is** — Evans states directly (U3 L6 p.6, slide titled "Body Composition Reality"): "Body composition analysis is NOT a measurement, it is a PREDICTION. Want to get the a [sic] true measurement of body fat? Carcass Analysis ....so you're telling me I have to be dead to get my body fat measured?" The following slides (p.7-9) list body-composition models (Two, Three, and Four Compartment) and the most widely used field methods (Hydrostatic Weighing, BodPod, DEXA, Bioelectrical Impedance, Skinfolds). The p.9 error-rate slide is laid out in three blocks: "Small Error Rates for Populations" - Underwater Weighing (UW) 0.1-2.1%, BodPod (BP) 2%, Skinfolds (SF) 6%, DEXA 1-2%; the slide also lists "Ethnicity, Age, Gender..." (no label); "Large Error Rates for Individuals" - UW 5%+, BP 6%+, Bioelectrical Impedance (BIA) 8-9% (BIA has no population-level figure; 8-9% is its only figure on this slide), Skinfolds 10-15%, DEXA 4-10%; and, set apart under its own heading, "Tracking over time... different? SF: 3-5%."  

=== claim--weight-room-transfer-limited-without-dynamic-correspondence.md
**What it is** — Evans states directly (U4 L1 p.5): "Most Important: Special Work Capacity... Movement & Energetic potential relative to the sporting demands. Primary Questions (Needs Analysis): What are the movements required? Dynamic Correspondence. What are the dominant energy systems fueling those movements? Weight room exercises? Provide little insight on how they will perform on their respective field of play. Why? Minimal DC criteria met." He then immediately qualifies this, anticipating pushback (p.5): "Whoa there. You saying the weight room is not important? Absolutely not!"  

=== framework--two-factors-special-work-capacity-technical-mastery.md
**What it is** — Evans's slide (U1 L3 p.14) states "THE TWO FACTORS to INCREASE SPORT RESULT" as "Special Work Capacity and Technical Mastery," defined in a two-column table: Special Work Capacity is "Motor potential (power generators) that are specific to the sport"; Technical Mastery is "Skills to coordinate maximal force efforts OR to rationally employ force efforts." No author or citation is given for this specific two-factor framing on this slide (contrast with the surrounding slides, which name Verkhoshansky and Anokhin explicitly). This exact framing recurs twice more in the course: verbatim as the opening slide of the Unit 4 summary lecture (U4 L3 p.2), and as the U4 L1 p.5 slide headed "Most Important: Special Work Capacity... Movement & Energetic potential relative to the sporting demands."  

=== framework--issurin-five-training-domains.md
**What it is** — Evans's slide "The Training Process" (U1 L3 p.15, repeated verbatim as "Training Domains" at U2 L4 p.4), cited to "(Issurin, 2008)," gives a five-row table of Domain and Purpose: Physical, "To improve physical (motor) abilities and increase the physiological potential of athletes"; Technical, "To acquire cognitive technical skills and attain the desired level of technical mastery"; Tactical, "To acquire cognitive sport-specific tactics, which allow for the most effective utilization of athlete's motor and technical abilities in competition"; Psychological, "To develop the athlete's personality so that it is harmonious, highly motivated and morally stable. To instill the skills of cognitive self-regulation of the athlete's emotional state in order to facilitate maximum realization of their psycho-physiological potential"; Intellectual, "To improve athletes' general and sport-specific knowledge in order to effectively complete their training and competitive program." No book title or page number is given beyond the year.  

=== framework--sport-specific-test-battery-model.md
**What it is** — Evans's slides (U3 L6) give two related pieces. First, "Assessment Considerations" (p.3): Athlete Preparation (diet, training, testing), Test Environment (surface, cleanliness, temperature, time of day), Test Order ("Non Physical -> Physical (High Velocity -> Low Velocity)"), and an Equipment Checklist & Assignments (per drill/activity: equipment required, test procedures, who is in charge of testing and data collection). Second, three worked sport-specific battery tables, each with a Test and a stated Rationale column (p.20-22): for Track Cyclists in a velodrome - Anthropometry (assess body composition), VO2Max ("Cyclists on Track are often characterized with high aerobic power"), Alactic Peak Power, 6s ("Examine the alactic power mechanism specific in the leg musculature"), 30-min Time Trial ("'Race of Truth'. No tactics involved (drafting)"), Movement Screen; for Basketball - Anthropometry (assess and compare against positional values), Vertical Jump ("common feature in offensive and defensive movements"), Sprints 5/10/20m (acceleration and speed), Right/Left Shuffle Line-to-Line Drill (anaerobic-glycolytic capacity), Yo-Yo Intermittent Test (aerobic capacity), 1-6RM Squat/Bench (maximal contractile qualities), Movement Screen; for Rowers - Anthropometry, a 7x4-min Incremental Test based on best 2000m time (submaximal capacity, efficiency, and training zones from lactate and HR data), 1-6RM Squat/Bench Pull/Clean (maximal strength qualities), Movement Screen.  

=== framework--monitoring-toolkit-by-domain-frequency-cost.md
**What it is** — Evans's slides (U4 L1 p.16-19) organize monitoring tools into four domains, each with named solutions and a suggested frequency, and (for two of the four) a relative cost tier ($ = Low/None, $$ = Moderate, $$$ = High). Nutrition/Body Composition: Bodyweight (weekly), Skinfolds (biweekly or monthly), Body Comp Analyzers - DEXA, Hydrostatic, InBody, BodPod (no more than 4x per year), Blood Biomarkers via a sports medicine hospital or LabCorp (3-4x per year, "focus on simple biomarkers, e.g. serum ferritin, D3"), with a stated minimum of "Performance metrics + Body Composition," and no cost tier given for this domain. Psychological: Profile of Mood States (monthly, $), Recovery-Stress Questionnaire for Athletes (weekly, $), Daily Analysis of Life Demands for Athletes (weekly, $), Smith Relaxation States Inventory (weekly, $), sRPE "used to calculate training load, monotony, strain" (daily, $), a custom soreness/sickness/lethargy questionnaire (daily-weekly, $) - all marked for team-sport use with checkmarks or "Best Athletes" only. Movement/Muscle: FMS, PCA, isolated muscle testing (e.g. groin squeeze), isolated joint ROM (e.g. total arc) - "Full screen during critical times, individual tests more frequently," no cost tier given. Physical Fitness: Jump Tests (Bosco, DJ-RSI, SJ, CMJ, "ES or 2x," $), Sprint Tests 10-20yds (1x, $), Weight Exercises via Linear Transducers (1-2x, $$-$$$), Player Tracking/GPS ("Every field based session," $$$), Aerobic Tests via Heart Rate Recovery (1x, $-$$), Training Load (sRPE x Duration, "Best athletes," ES, $), Monotony (Aver

=== claim--big-data-monitoring-without-training-theory-is-noise.md
**What it is** — Evans's slide (U4 L2 p.5) quotes Carl Valle directly: "Monitoring instead of creating insight to the responses of athletes to training, is now creating a data and information dark age in regards to the understanding of training, by poorly appreciating the basic principles." And: "Without fully comprehending the training process, monitoring is nothing more than observational recordings of a suicide mission, resulting in ornamental data displayed real time for coaches to find a purpose because they are too fearful to train." No publication or year is given for the quote beyond the name "Carl Valle." The surrounding slides name a five-step "ACQUIRE, MANAGE, ANALYZE, VISUALIZE, ACTION" pipeline (p.6) and list "Practical Reasons to Monitor" as Athlete Feedback, Coach Feedback, and Medical Team/Return to Play (p.8); p.9-20 are equipment and product images (Catapult, timing gates, Omegawave, BioForce, ithlete, Haloview dashboard, Firstbeat/Polar, Noraxon, Dartfish, and similar vendor photos and video stills) with no argument text.  

=== heuristic--monitoring-is-a-compass-not-a-gps.md
**What it is** — Evans's closing slide (U4 L1 p.23, "closing thoughts") states (no attribution shown): "Monitoring is a compass, not a GPS unit. Only utilize it if you believe in the literature and will utilize it to make adjustments to the training process. Start simple and small, but be very consistent.
